title: Establish cross-SDK defaults and taxonomy for retries, backoff, and idempotency
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a single, pragmatic specification that all Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) will implement for: default retry/backoff parameters, idempotency key semantics for mutating endpoints, and a canonical retryable error taxonomy. Goal is to reduce customer confusion, minimize surprising behavior across languages, and provide safe defaults for streaming and non-streaming flows.
background: We currently have divergent retry behaviors across SDKs: different default retry counts, inconsistent header names for idempotency, and edge cases with streamed responses. Downstream teams report customer confusion and duplicated docs. This ticket consolidates decisions so SDKs can ship consistent examples and automated tests.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document accepted by SDK leads (Python, TS, Go) and API team
SDKs implement defaults and pass cross-language conformance tests
Updated examples showing idempotent create semantics and streaming guidance in docs
Migration notes for customers with existing retry behavior
proposed_defaults: Retry policy: 3 total retries (i.e., original + 3 retry attempts) for idempotent/unary requests
Backoff: exponential with base 100ms, multiplier 2.0, max interval 2s, full-jitter
Max elapsed time (per request): 10s (includes all retries); SDKs expose client-level override
Retryable gRPC statuses: Unavailable(14), DeadlineExceeded(4), ResourceExhausted(8) when server-side throttling suspected
Idempotency header: use 'Idempotency-Key' for user-specified idempotency; SDKs auto-generate 'X-RW-Idempotency' for internal retries when user does not provide key

Mutating endpoints: default to requiring user-supplied Idempotency-Key for retries when operation is non-idempotent by design (e.g., create-resource). SDKs will automatically attach a generated idempotency key for best-effort retry of client-initiated requests, but document the trade-offs

Streaming: by default, streaming responses are NOT retried. SDKs must expose a resumable streaming API only when server supports resume tokens; otherwise SDKs should surface a descriptive error and a 'retryable_in_full' flag to callers
Telemetry: SDKs emit metrics/events for each retry attempt and final outcome (succeeded-after-retry, exhausted-retries, non-retriable-failure)
open_questions: Should SDKs surface 'attempt number' in callback contexts for streaming partial-results?
When server returns 500 vs 502/503, do we allow retries for 500 if error body contains 'transient' hint?
Should the auto-generated idempotency key be stable across process restarts for exactly-once semantics, or ephemeral per-request? (proposal: ephemeral per-request)
How to handle user-supplied non-UUID idempotency keys (length/charset limits) across language SDKs?
design-decisions: Full-jitter chosen to avoid thundering-herd; base/backoff values tuned for typical Redwood hosted latency distribution
Limit retries to keep user-visible latency bounded and avoid masking application bugs; expose overrides for power users
Streaming operations considered fundamentally different: do not retry by default to avoid duplication and state confusion
Use standard header 'Idempotency-Key' to align with common ecosystem practices; vendor header 'X-RW-Idempotency' reserved for SDK-generated keys to aid debugging
implementation-tasks: Python SDK: add RetryPolicy class + default wiring, emit telemetry metrics; update docs/examples
TypeScript SDK: unify backoff config naming with Python (backoffBaseMs/backoffMultiplier/maxBackoffMs/maxElapsedMs); add IdempotencyKey helper
Go SDK: expose RetryConfig struct with context-aware cancellation; implement generated idempotency header helper
Test: cross-language conformance harness with mocked transient errors and streaming non-retry asserts
Docs: write migration guide and examples (create-with-idempotency, resumable-streaming-example, retry-tuning)
risk-tradeoffs: Auto-generating idempotency keys improves reliability but may create surprising duplicate resources if servers treat keys differently; mitigation: clearly document server semantics and surface idempotency key in logs
Allowing retries on 500 with heuristic increases success rate but risks masking application/server correctness issues; default disabled, allow opt-in
Not retrying streams by default may frustrate users on flaky networks; mitigation: provide resumable streaming API and examples
examples: Python: client.create_completion(prompt, idempotency_key='user-12345') # safe to retry
TS: const resp = await client.completions.create({ prompt }, { idempotencyKey: uuidV4() })
Streaming guidance: use server-provided resume_token to continue stream from last ack; SDK will surface ResumeStream(resume_token) helper when supported
